launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.address: 233 South Civic Center Drive, Columbus, OH 43215
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.summary: A connected downtown riverfront of parks, promenades, bridges, fountains, lawns, public art and trails along the Scioto River.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.hours: Outdoor riverfront parks are generally open daily; individual fountains, restrooms, events and reservable spaces keep shorter or seasonal schedules.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.parking: Use downtown meters and garages near Civic Center Drive, Rich Street, Main Street or North Bank. Event and festival closures can change the closest approach.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.arrival: The Scioto Mile is a corridor, not one pin. Choose Bicentennial Park and the fountain, Genoa Park, North Bank Park or a bridge crossing before parking.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.restrooms: Public restrooms are concentrated near major park buildings and event areas and can be seasonal. Plan around Bicentennial Park or a nearby downtown facility.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.cost: The parks, promenade, fountain viewing and trails are free. Parking, concessions, reservations and ticketed events cost separately.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.accessibility: Broad paved promenades and bridge connections serve the riverfront, though construction, flooding and event barriers can interrupt a route.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome on ordinary paths and lawns; keep pets out of the interactive fountain and crowded events.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.family: The seasonal fountain and broad riverfront paths are the strongest family draws. Verify fountain operation before bringing swim clothes.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.transit: COTA buses and downtown bikeways serve the riverfront; several attractions are a short walk from Broad, High and Main streets.
launch-oh-columbus-scioto-mile.need: The interactive fountain is seasonal and weather-dependent. Scioto River flooding, festivals and construction can close segments independently.

launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.summary: A historic east-side park surrounding Franklin Park Conservatory, with formal gardens, community gardens, cascades, lawns, trails and recreation facilities.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.hours: Outdoor park grounds are generally open daily. Franklin Park Conservatory, Children's Garden and staffed facilities use separate admission and operating hours.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.parking: Free surface parking serves the conservatory and park, but conservatory exhibitions, weddings and the Asian Festival can fill the closest lots.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.arrival: Choose the Conservatory and Children's Garden, Community Garden Campus, Cascades, amphitheater or adaptive sports complex before arriving; Broad Street is the clearest landmark.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.restrooms: Reliable restrooms are inside ticketed or staffed facilities during their hours; outdoor and event facilities vary.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.cost: Franklin Park grounds are free. Conservatory admission, exhibitions, classes and special events may require tickets.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.accessibility: Main garden and conservatory approaches are paved, and the adaptive sports complex is purpose-built; lawn and garden surfaces vary.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor park areas but not inside the conservatory or children's garden except service animals.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.family: The Children's Garden is a major family attraction but belongs to the ticketed conservatory experience; the surrounding park remains free.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.transit: COTA service runs along East Broad Street near the main entrance.
launch-oh-columbus-franklin-park.need: Do not assume park hours or free park access include the conservatory. The Palm House, Davis Showhouse and Wolfe Terrace are closed for renovation until fall 2027, and Sandstone Creek in the Children's Garden is temporarily closed; check current tickets, exhibitions and event-day parking.

launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.summary: A historic Short North park with pond, fountain, mature trees, playground, courts, shelterhouse, gardens and neighborhood paths.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.hours: The outdoor park is generally available daily; shelterhouse, restroom, court and event access may keep separate schedules.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.parking: Street parking surrounds the park, with garages in the Short North. Festivals and weekend dining traffic can make the north and east sides difficult.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.arrival: Use Goodale Street for the pond and shelterhouse side or Park Street for the Short North edge; pick a feature before circling for parking.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.restrooms: Restroom availability is centered near the shelterhouse and can be seasonal or event-dependent.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.cost: Park, playground, paths and ordinary court use are free. Parking, shelter reservations and permitted events cost separately.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.accessibility: Paved paths reach major developed areas, but older paths, turf and pond edges vary.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome; this is not an off-leash dog park.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.family: The playground, pond and open lawns make an easy central-city family stop, with food nearby in the Short North.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.transit: High Street buses and neighborhood bikeways stop within a short walk.
launch-oh-columbus-goodale-park.need: ComFest and other large events transform access and parking. The pond is ornamental and not for swimming or wading.

launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.summary: German Village's historic community park with stage, fountain, recreation center, playground, courts, gardens, pond, lawns and neighborhood paths.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.hours: Park grounds are generally open daily. The recreation center, stage programs, restrooms and reservable areas use separate hours.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.parking: Free neighborhood street parking is the normal approach. Shakespeare performances, festivals and busy weekends can fill nearby blocks.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.arrival: Jaeger Street is useful for the recreation center and central park; choose the stage, fountain, playground or garden as the meeting point.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.restrooms: Restrooms are associated with the recreation center and seasonal park operations; confirm building hours for reliable access.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.cost: Park, playground, gardens and ordinary court use are free. Classes, reservations and selected performances or events may charge or request donations.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.accessibility: Paved neighborhood paths reach major amenities, while grass, older garden routes and performance seating surfaces vary.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary outdoor areas; keep them out of playground equipment and organized events when posted.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.family: Playground, pond, lawns and summer theater make this a useful family stop within German Village.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.transit: COTA routes serve nearby German Village streets, followed by a neighborhood walk.
launch-oh-columbus-schiller-park.need: Theater and festival schedules can occupy the stage lawn. Schiller's playground is part of an active city improvement cycle, so check posted construction conditions.

launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.summary: A large Clintonville park best known for the free Columbus Park of Roses, with formal gardens, prairie, playground, courts, fields and Olentangy Trail access.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.hours: Outdoor park and garden areas are generally open daily. Garden bloom, restrooms, athletic facilities and reserved events are seasonal or separately scheduled.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.parking: Free lots serve Whetstone Park and the Park of Roses. Peak rose bloom, weddings and community events can fill the garden-side spaces.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.arrival: Use the Park of Roses entrance for formal gardens, or route directly to the prairie, playground, courts or Olentangy Trail connection.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.restrooms: Restrooms are concentrated near developed park and garden facilities and may be seasonal.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.cost: The park, Park of Roses, prairie, playground and trails are free. Reservations, classes and special events may cost separately.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.accessibility: Paved garden paths and developed park routes provide broad access; prairie, turf and trail surfaces vary.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.dogs: Leashed dogs are welcome in ordinary park areas; protect formal beds and follow garden event restrictions.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.family: The playground and open park pair well with a short garden walk, but children should stay out of planting beds.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.transit: North High Street bus service stops near Whetstone, and the Olentangy Trail provides bicycle access.
launch-oh-columbus-whetstone-park-and-co.need: Peak rose bloom usually draws the largest crowds but varies with weather. The garden is free and outdoors; weddings may reserve focal areas without closing the entire park.

launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.summary: A 1,204-acre Metro Park with 100-foot shale bluffs, deep ravines, river overlooks, nature center, natural play, picnic areas and varied trails.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.hours: April 1-September 30: 6:30 a.m.-10:00 p.m. October 1-March 31: 6:30 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Nature Center: 9:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. in summer and 9:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in winter.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.parking: Free lots serve the Nature Center, Big Meadows, Oak Coves, River Bluff and trail areas. Navigate to the exact area rather than the general park pin.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.arrival: Use the Nature Center for exhibits, Big Meadows for playgrounds and natural play, or the named Overlook, Dripping Rock and Scenic River trailheads.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.restrooms: ADA restrooms serve the Nature Center and developed picnic areas; some shelter-area restrooms are seasonal.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.cost: Park admission, parking, trails, nature center and first-come picnic shelters are free. Reservations and programs may vary.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.accessibility: The Nature Center, Scenic River and Sycamore trails and picnic facilities offer accessible options; Overlook and Dripping Rock are hillier gravel routes.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed on designated pet trails and in picnic and parking areas, but not every preserve trail.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.family: Big Meadows combines playgrounds, playfields, picnic shelters and a 15-acre natural play area; the Nature Center is a strong weather backup.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.transit: Regional transit is limited; driving or cycling is practical for most visitors.
launch-oh-columbus-highbanks-metro-park.need: The Overlook Trail is a moderate-to-difficult 2.3-mile route to a deck 100 feet above the Olentangy. Stay on trail in the state nature preserve.

launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.summary: A 7,358-acre Metro Park along two scenic rivers with bison pastures, a living-stream nature center, prairies, wetlands, natural play, trails and paddling access.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.hours: April 1-September 30: 6:30 a.m.-10:00 p.m. October 1-March 31: 6:30 a.m.-8:00 p.m. Nature Center: 9:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. in summer and 9:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. in winter.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.parking: Free lots are spread among the Nature Center, Indian Ridge, Cedar Ridge, canoe area, Osprey Lake and Pleasant Valley. Select the exact area first.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.arrival: The Nature Center and bison pastures are the simplest first visit. Indian Ridge serves natural play; paddling and southern trail areas use separate entrances.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.restrooms: Restrooms serve the Nature Center and major picnic areas, while remote trails and access points have limited facilities.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.cost: Park, parking, trails, bison viewing and nature center are free. Reservations and organized programs may vary.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.accessibility: The Nature Center and selected greenway and picnic routes are accessible; natural trails, creek banks and prairie surfaces vary.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.dogs: Leashed dogs are allowed on designated pet trails and developed areas; keep well away from bison fencing and wildlife.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.family: The living stream in the Nature Center, bison viewing and nine-acre natural play area make a strong family sequence.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.transit: There is little practical public transit to the distributed park entrances; driving is recommended.
launch-oh-columbus-battelle-darby-creek-.need: Bison roam two enclosed pastures and may be distant or temporarily out of view. Never cross fencing or approach wildlife; bring binoculars.

launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.summary: A reclaimed 182-acre quarry with a 25-foot waterfall, lakes, paved paths, mountain biking, dog park, paddling, sport climbing and reservation-only via ferrata.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.hours: Open year-round from 6:30 a.m. until dark. Programs, climbing access and construction areas may use separate schedules.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.parking: Use 2158 Old Dublin Road for Millikin Falls, 2600 Dublin Road for the north area and mountain biking, or 2319 Quarry Trails Drive for the lake area.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.arrival: Do not use one general pin. Choose Waterfall Entrance, Northern Area or Lake Area before driving; they do not function as one compact lot.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.restrooms: Restrooms and portable facilities are available in developed areas, but coverage varies while the park continues to develop.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.cost: Park, parking, trails, waterfall, dog park and ordinary lake access are free. Via ferrata requires a guided program reservation; climbers provide required gear for sport routes.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.accessibility: The paved North-South Connector includes an ADA boardwalk from Lake Area parking. Waterfall steps, bike routes and climbing areas are not universally accessible.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.dogs: Leashed pets are welcome on designated paths, and a two-acre fenced dog park separates small and large dogs; running water is not guaranteed there.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.family: The waterfall overlook, lakes and paved paths work for general visits. Climbing and mountain-bike areas require age, skill, gear and supervision appropriate to the activity.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.transit: Transit is limited at the separated entrances; driving or cycling is usually simplest.
launch-oh-columbus-quarry-trails-metro-p.need: Via ferrata access is guided and reservation-only, for visitors at least 14, at least five feet tall and 88-265 pounds. The 90-minute route includes elevated cable crossings.
